text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Reasons why Macedonian stocks do not sell and why there is only occasional trade on the Macedonian Stock Exchange are unfinished privatisation, fear of publishing business and financial results and still undefined legal regulations.

- Macedonia suffers major decrease of maize crop in all production regions, according to experts. In the region of Pelagonia alone instead of expected 45,000 tonnes, only 36,000 tonnes have been harvested. Bread prices will not rise and state reserves and imports will compensate the flour-milling industry's needs.

- Government spokesman Zoran Ivanov renounced as speculation media claims that the government would demand the country's exclusion from U.N. membership. Government estimates that it is pure insinuation to claim that the U.N. Security Council would rename the state "Republic of New Macedonia".

- The ruling SDSM party claims that after summer holidays it will propose the first version of electoral laws and all political parties will be able to give their suggestions. Daily Nova Makedonija speculates elections will be held in March or April 1998 the earliest.

- MAAK Conservative party announced celebration of Macedonian national holiday Ilinden in the Prohor Pcinjski monastery in Serbia. The party said it received information from the Macedonian embassy in Belgrade that the Yugoslav government will issue its approval for the celebration.

- Opposition Macedonian parties claim that the huge publicity given to the possible renaming of Macedonia by the U.N. Security Council is proof that back stage, the Greek and Macedonian governments are preparing the public opinion for something that will happen soon.

- Macedonian Economy Minister Boris Rikalovski and Yugoslav Ambassador to Skopje Zoran Janackovic discussed implementation of bilateral free-trade agreement. Questions for resolving property-legal regulations also raised.
- According to the latest study on protection of waters in Macedonia, one billion German marks are needed for water purification. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
